extracted.intended_audience: general readers, students, creative-writing instructors, and aspiring writers
extracted.subtask_description: An encyclopedic overview of the creative writing field, covering definitions, pedagogy, program structure, classroom practices, program outcomes, and core elements of creative writing craft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on craft and technique
rubrics_metrics.description: Creative writing is typically identified by an emphasis on craft and technique, such as narrative structure, character development, literary tropes, genre, and poetics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to distinguish creative writing from professional, journalistic, academic, or technical forms of literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original composition (originality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Creative writing can technically be considered any writing of original composition; in this sense, creative writing is a contemporary and process-oriented name for what has been traditionally called literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original composition is presented as a core definitional criterion for creative writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-expression and personal needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Creative writing is a composition of any type of writing at any time primarily in the service of such needs as the need for keeping records of significant experience, the need for sharing experience with an interested group, and the need for free individual expression which contributes to mental and physical health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames creative writing as serving personal and communal expressive needs (quoted from Marksberry via Witty and LaBrant).

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshop format / peer critique
rubrics_metrics.description: Creative writing is usually taught in a workshop format, where students submit original work for peer critique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Workshop setting is presented as the common pedagogical vehicle; peer feedback is central.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing process: practice of writing and re-writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Students also develop a writing process through the practice of writing and re-writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revision and iterative practice are core procedures for developing craft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching technical issues (editing, narrative structure, techniques)
rubrics_metrics.description: Courses may teach the means to exploit or access latent creativity, and may teach more technical issues such as editing, narrative structure, literary techniques, genres, idea generation, or overcoming writer's block.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists typical technical syllabus components instructors may cover.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program scheduling: reading assignments, regular writing tasks, workshops
rubrics_metrics.description: Students make a schedule based on emphasis, including reading assignments, regular writing tasks, and workshops to strengthen their skills, knowledge and techniques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended structure for coursework in creative-writing programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extracurricular engagement (publishing, contests, colonies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Creative writing students are encouraged to get involved in extracurricular writing-based activities, such as publishing clubs, school literary magazines or newspapers, writing contests, writing colonies or conventions, and extended education classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation outside class is presented as complementary to classroom learning and skill development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Developing resilience, empathy, and psychological benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Many educators find that using creative writing can increase students' academic performance and psychological resilience; completing small goals engenders pride, increases motivation, and helps students document and analyze experiences, building resilience and compassion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes documented/purported beneficial outcomes of creative-writing practice for students' well-being and social skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefits for international and multilingual students
rubrics_metrics.description: Creative writing may develop international students into better readers, analysts, and writers, encouraging them to express and connect their heritage and experiences across languages and contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarizes case-study evidence that creative writing can boost confidence and cross-linguistic transfer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Developing narrative voice and transferable skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Creative-writing pedagogy can help students develop their own unique writing style and voice, empathy, self-awareness, and narrative voice; these skills are transferable to other real-world situations such as professional settings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrasts creative-writing pedagogy with heavy academic-writing focus and highlights transferability of creative skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility and inclusivity in pedagogy
rubrics_metrics.description: The pedagogy of creative writing is criticized for methods that may discriminate against people with disabilities, emphasizing practices such as daily writing requirements or location-based writing that students with chronic illnesses or neurodivergency are unable to access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implies a criterion that creative-writing instruction should be designed to be accessible and inclusive; warns against exclusive practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity and selection of texts (canon critique)
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection of texts used in traditional creative writing programs has been criticized as historically rooted and linked to exclusion and structural racism in creative writing programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Points toward a curricular criterion favoring diverse and inclusive text selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prison program aims: education, structure, creative outlet, rehabilitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Creative writing programs in prisons aim to provide education, structure, and a creative outlet to encourage rehabilitation of prisoners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs rely on volunteers and external support; they are framed as rehabilitative interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prison program outcomes: self-esteem, social connection, skills, reentry
rubrics_metrics.description: Workshops and classes in prisons help prisoners build self-esteem, make healthy social connections, learn new skills, and ease prisoner reentry; improved writing skills can enhance abilities in other academic areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists empirical/observed benefits from studies of prison creative-writing programs.
